blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — postpartum oxytocin for uterine atony
stem: After delivery of the placenta, a postpartum client has uterine atony with increased bleeding. Why is oxytocin administered?

options.A: To provide analgesia for postpartum perineal pain and uterine cramping after delivery.
options.B: To stimulate uterine contractions, improve uterine tone, and control bleeding caused by uterine atony.
options.C: To prevent postpartum venous thromboembolism in a client with major clotting risk factors.
options.D: To treat severe postpartum hypertension and reduce the risk of maternal stroke after delivery.

rationale: Oxytocin acts directly on uterine smooth muscle to stimulate rhythmic contractions and increase uterine tone. Current FDA labeling states that postpartum oxytocin is indicated to produce uterine contractions and control postpartum bleeding or hemorrhage, and its postpartum dosing section specifically describes administration to control uterine atony. Therefore B directly explains the therapeutic purpose in this client. A, C, and D describe legitimate postpartum treatment goals, but oxytocin is not being administered for analgesia, venous-thromboembolism prophylaxis, or hypertension treatment.
educational_objective: Explain that postpartum oxytocin treats uterine atony by stimulating uterine contractions and increasing tone, thereby helping control postpartum bleeding.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_version_date: DailyMed updated January 12, 2026; labeling revised July 2023; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Clinical Pharmacology; Indications and Usage — Postpartum; Dosage and Administration — Control of Postpartum Uterine Bleeding.
source_claim_supported: Oxytocin stimulates uterine smooth muscle, increases contraction frequency and tone, is indicated postpartum to produce uterine contractions and control postpartum bleeding or hemorrhage, and is dosed for control of postpartum uterine atony.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: prepare and administer medications using rights of medication administration; review pertinent data prior to medication administration; evaluate client response to medication.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices to substantive postpartum treatment goals of comparable length.
Retained only one oxytocin-specific indication in the option set, eliminating the original answer-length cue without changing the clinical construct.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms B is the only option that matches the labeled postpartum purpose of oxytocin in uterine atony. The distractors are plausible postpartum care goals but do not represent oxytocin indications, and revised lengths no longer cue the key.
